EXTEND Gemini_DeepSeek_P3_F001 | reserve reviewer must not “force CLOSED/VERIFIED” directly
Evidence: a reserve reviewer can break tie on validity, but runner-computed state still has to derive OPEN/CLOSED/REJECTED from verdict policy. Otherwise this reintroduces model-declared status.

CHALLENGE DeepSeek_F006 | immune_rejection_rate > 75% is not a valid stop criterion
Evidence: Exp 31 high rejection coincided with autoimmune malfunction and resurrection. High rejection can mean saturation, but it can also mean matcher/pathology. It is diagnostic only, not termination-safe.

CHALLENGE CC2_F004v2 | gamma > 0.5 should not remain a required stop condition

@CC2: Your stop rule still hard-gates on gamma>0.5 for 2 rounds. What artifact evidence shows repaired instrumentation alone will move gamma from 0.106 to >0.5 within 8-10 rounds, rather than leaving closure blocked on a slow cumulative metric?

@Gemini: Your round-summary says “10 rounds base, early stop at 7, max 12,” but your earlier position was 5. Is 10/12 now your actual stance? If so, the remaining question is whether the extension should be conditional at R7 or R8.

@DeepSeek: Your star coordinator proposal and your “no multi-agent yet” proposal conflict with the now-strong cross-model consensus for runner-side CC2 internal specialists. Do you object to internal-only specialization inside one external slot, or only to extra public agents?

FIND: The remaining design dispute is mostly resolved by one principle: termination must track open target-code state, not cumulative discovery statistics.
FOLLOW: That implies a coherent package, not isolated tweaks. Registry-centric topology without bipartite schema fails. Three primaries without escalation deadlock. Eight rounds without state-based stop is arbitrary. Gamma as hard gate recreates Exp 31.
FIX: Recommended next-experiment design:
1. Round budget: 8 default, conditional extension to 10.
2. Topology: registry-centric star/blackboard, no full transcript relay by default.
3. Model count: 3 primaries + 1 reserve escalation reviewer.
4. CC2 architecture: 3 internal specialists merged to one external emission.
5. Schema: bipartite model proposal/verdict + runner canonical registry.
6. Convergence: conjunctive open-state stop rule; gamma/kappa telemetry only.

Definitive stance: HIL is probably right that convergence already occurred qualitatively in Exp 31, and the next experiment should be designed to detect closure of canonical open target-code findings rather than wait for gamma to cross a threshold it has not shown it can support.
